title: How Britain Built Two Harbours in Secret and Floated Them to Normandy
description_draft:
Britain built the Mulberry harbours in sections and towed them to Normandy to supply the D-Day armies.

00:00 The problem on the beaches
05:09 A pier that follows the tide
09:48 Building a harbour in pieces
13:57 The Channel tow
18:37 The June storm
22:47 Fuel and the tonnage verdict

Sources: SHAEF Chief Engineers' Report on Artificial Harbours (*Mulberry A & B*, UK The National Archives `CAB 106/999` & `WO 219/2522`, 1945); Winston Churchill, *"Piers for Use on Beaches"* minute (`30 May 1942`, UK TNA `PREM 3/216/1`); Roland G. Ruppenthal, *Logistical Support of the Armies, Vol. I: May 1941 – September 1944* (US Army Center of Military History, 1953, pp. 392–432); Samuel Eliot Morison, *History of United States Naval Operations in World War II, Vol. XI: The Invasion of France and Germany, 1944–1945* (Little, Brown, 1957, pp. 161–178); Institution of Civil Engineers, *The Civil Engineer in War, Vol. 2: Docks and Harbours* (ICE London, 1948 — papers by Wood, Beckett, Jory, Pavry, and Lochner); Guy Hartcup, *Code Name Mulberry: The Planning, Building & Operation of the Normandy Harbours* (David & Charles, 1977 / Pen & Sword, 2011).
